newsitem.title: USA: U.S. venture funding hit a record $10.1 billion.
newsitem.headline: U.S. venture funding hit a record $10.1 billion.

text.p: Venture capital firms invested a record $10.1 billion in 1996 as venture funding of small start-up companies rose a whopping 52 percent from record 1995 levels, according to a study by Coopers and Lybrand LLP.

The accounting firm said Wednesday that its Money Tree Survey found venture capital firms participated in 2,163 deals in 1996, 40 percent more than were funded in the previous year. The average size of deals financed rose to $4.7 million last year from $4.3 million in 1995.

"The fourth quarter of 1996 continued to show strong momentum in venture capital investing," Coopers & Lybrand said, noting 571 deals worth $2.6 billion were completed in the fourth quarter. That was up from $2.3 billion in the third quarter, when the July stock market setback cooled deal-making.
James Atwell, who heads Coopers & Lybrand's San Jose, Calif.-based venture capital group, said the hot initial public offering market of 1996 helped venture investors produce significant returns.
"There's every indication that this trend will continue into 1997," said Atwell, noting that venture partnerships have raised record levels of capital for the last three years.
Atwell cited an abundance of startup Internet companies and networking and communications operations, along with consolidation in the healthcare sector as factors that helped fuel many of the deals.

Venture capital firms, many of which are based in the San Francisco Bay Area, invest in small, emerging companies that are expected to produce rapid growth and returns for the investment and endowment funds, companies and wealthy individuals who bankroll them.

California accounted for the major portion of venture funding commitments in 1996, with deals worth $3.2 billion, up 49 percent from the prior year, while Massachusetts was second, nearly doubling its total to more than $1 billion.
Texas was third with $596 million, followed by Colorado with $393 million and Florida with $376 million.

Technology-based companies received about 60 percent of total venture capital investment in 1996, with software companies alone accounting for 16 percent of the total value invested, a rise of 112 percent from 1995 levels.
Communications companies were nearly even with software, rising 50 percent to $1.6 billion, and healthcare investments rose 104 percent to $1.1 billion.

During the fourth quarter, California accounted for $803 million, or 31 percent of investment dollars, followed by Massachusets and Texas. The communications sector drew the most investment in the fourth quarter, with $496 million, 20 percent of the quarter's investment dollars.
